justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are met: R-01 and R-02 are supported via 'Azure Static Web Apps' and 'Claim Processing Domain Services'; R-03 is facilitated through 'Azure API Management' policy routing and 'Claim Migration Topic & Subscriptions' to enable incremental claim-type migrations.
justifications.performance_efficiency: R-05 is achieved as 'Mainframe Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) Adapter' and 'Azure Service Bus' decouple frontend requests from 5s mainframe latencies. Serving adjuster views locally from 'Azure SQL Database' via 'API Gateway / BFF' ensures sub-2-second response times.
justifications.compatibility: Interoperability is thoroughly addressed: 'Azure Entra ID' federates with the insurer's on-premises Active Directory for SSO, while 'Azure Service Bus' and 'Azure API Management' coexist cleanly with the 'On-Premises COBOL/DB2 Mainframe' over mTLS and ExpressRoute.
justifications.usability: All target user groups (End Customers, Brokers, Claims Adjusters) are explicitly served through specialized interfaces delivered by 'Azure Static Web Apps', featuring 'SPA Router & View Modules' and unified authentication via 'Auth & Session Manager'.
justifications.reliability: R-04 consistency targets are satisfied by 'Mainframe Sync Queue' with duplicate detection, partitioned queues, and transactional handling. 'Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ)' safely captures messages rejected during nightly batch windows, while 'Azure Stream Analytics' executes validation checks.
justifications.security: Strong security mechanisms are defined: SSO via 'Azure Entra ID', edge JWT validation in 'Azure API Management', mTLS over ExpressRoute, and data protection via 'Row-Level Security & Access Management', 'Temporal Tables', and 'Azure Key Vault'.
justifications.maintainability: R-06 switch-back within one day is well enabled by 'Configuration & Feature Flag Service' and 'APIM Policy Engine Component'. However, excessive Azure architectural complexity (AKS, Synapse, Event Hubs) places a heavy burden on a team with little cloud experience.
justifications.portability: The hybrid topology (on-premises mainframe and Azure West Europe) matches constraints, and core services run on containerized runtimes in 'Azure Kubernetes Service'. However, tight coupling to proprietary Azure PaaS (APIM, Service Bus, Synapse) limits portability across environments.

PERF-01.justification: CQRS domain services and asynchronous synchronization isolate adjusters from mainframe latency. However, if a claim requires un-cached real-time data from the legacy backend, direct APIM-to-mainframe routing may exceed the 2-second limit without explicit read-caching mechanisms.
sensitivity_points: Pre-synchronization freshness of legacy claims in Azure SQL
Latency of synchronous fallbacks to the mainframe
tradeoffs: Eventual consistency of claim views versus strict real-time accuracy

PERF-02.justification: Peak claim submissions are ingested asynchronously through API Management into Azure Service Bus queues and Azure SQL. The decoupled architecture buffers spikes, shielding the on-premises mainframe and preventing interference with the fixed nightly batch window.
sensitivity_points: Queue depth and partition limits during peak load
Throttling rate of messages forwarded to mainframe
tradeoffs: Buffering latency during peaks versus mainframe protection

AVAIL-01.justification: During the batch window, online submissions continue unabated via the modern platform. Azure Service Bus partitioning and dedicated Dead-Letter Queues hold and throttle sync messages, dispatching them reliably once the mainframe batch window closes.
sensitivity_points: Service Bus retention periods during batch window downtimes
Lockout schedule coordination between cloud and mainframe
tradeoffs: Queue operational cost versus lossless legacy decoupling

AVAIL-02.justification: The architecture incorporates duplicate detection in Service Bus, CDC staging, temporal tables in Azure SQL for state versioning, and serverless Azure Functions alongside Stream Analytics to detect anomalies and reconcile interrupted synchronization transactions.
sensitivity_points: Idempotency of synchronization messages and reconciliation logic
Accuracy of CDC tracking on integration tables
tradeoffs: Storage overhead of temporal tracking versus guaranteed auditability

MOD-01.justification: APIM policy-based routing, frontend feature flags, and Service Bus pub/sub topics allow fine-grained routing per claim type. The Anti-Corruption Layer isolates mainframe schema changes, and routing policies enable instant switch-back to the legacy system within a day.
sensitivity_points: Flexibility of dynamic APIM XML routing rules
Bi-directional data synchronization during rollback scenarios
tradeoffs: Dual-writing overhead versus instant rollback capability

MOD-02.justification: The frontend SPA connects exclusively to APIM and modern BFF services. The mainframe is isolated behind the ACL and integration queues. Decommissioning the mainframe simply involves turning off the ACL adapter without requiring any modifications to the adjuster or customer UIs.
sensitivity_points: Clean separation between BFF API contracts and legacy data formats
Readiness of Azure SQL to become primary system of record
tradeoffs: BFF abstraction complexity versus UI architectural stability

SEC-01.justification: APIM validates tokens and enforces access rules at the perimeter. Within the database, Row-Level Security restricts broker access to authorized customer records only, while Azure SQL Auditing and Application Insights record all authorization events and denial attempts.
sensitivity_points: Correct implementation of tenant/broker identifiers in JWTs
Row-Level Security rule coverage on transactional tables
tradeoffs: RLS query execution overhead versus centralized data authorization

SEC-02.justification: Revoking the adjuster in Active Directory/Entra ID immediately disables single sign-on access to the web UI and APIM gateway. Because adjusters interact with legacy data exclusively via the platform, mainframe access is effectively cut, though JWT token lifetime must be strictly tuned.
sensitivity_points: Access token expiration TTL and revocation evaluation
Propagation time between on-premises AD and Azure Entra ID
tradeoffs: Frequent token re-validation overhead versus rapid revocation guarantees

elements: Insurer Active Directory / Azure Entra ID
